codex_note:
## Codex runtime mapping

This published workflow is explicit-only through `agents/openai.yaml`. Use the native Codex subagent capability for independent read-only reviewers only when delegation is authorized. Require one immutable scope and rubric, at least two distinct model requests accepted by native spawn, separate read-only outputs, and a coordinator lead judgment before claiming a bounded review. If a configured reviewer is missing or fails, mark the aggregate PARTIAL and name the slot; never fabricate multi-model consensus or a complete configured run. Follow the standing `model-capability-router` and the operator-selected model/effort; do not force the Cursor default model table. Record requested reviewer profiles and unavailable slots, and mark effective model/effort readback unavailable unless the native surface supplies it. Keep the source rubric, lead judgment, and no-auto-apply contract.
codex_rule: Preserve independent review and source rubric while respecting native model, scope and permissions.
preserved_requirement: Use for "interrogate", "adversarial review", "multi-model review", "challenge this", "stress test this code", "find blind spots", or "tear this apart". Multiple LLM reviewers challenge changes from independent angles.
proof: Pinned source hash and deterministic build establish provenance. A disposable same-scope review produced two independent read-only reviewer executions, separate reports, consensus deduplication and lead judgment with no auto-apply. A separate exact PR #66 same-diff review produced four accepted findings corrected in 4e4139a0. Native spawn accepted two distinct requested profiles but the surface exposes no authoritative effective model/effort readback, so backend diversity is unverified. The bounded explicit-only review is published with PARTIAL on missing configured reviewers; automatic host trigger and full default four-reviewer coverage remain unproven. A separate native dropout on 5f040667 interrupted one configured slot; aggregate PARTIAL named it, retained only the survivor report, and made no edit.
reason: Replace Cursor Task and model config with native bounded reviewers while retaining the adversarial judgment workflow.

Use the actual available reviewers under the standing `model-capability-router` and the operator-selected model/effort; extend or shrink Reviewer A/B/C/D labels to match. Record unavailable reviewer slots.

replacements.after:

- Use a genuinely read-only role or instructions and verify no reviewer modified the workspace.
- Use native model selection only as allowed by the standing router and operator.

replacements.before: If a model slug is rejected as unresolvable when you try to spawn the subagent, check the valid slugs in the Task tool's error message, pick the closest equivalent (prefer the highest-reasoning tier of the same family), spawn with the valid slug, and open a separate PR to update the configured value or default table. Do not block the review on the slug issue. If the configured value is `inherit-parent` or `auto`, omit `model` instead. Never treat those aliases as broken slugs or enter this fallback for them.
replacements.after: If a requested model is unavailable, record that reviewer as unavailable. Continue with authorized available reviewers only when the proof bar can still be met. Do not silently substitute a model or create a repair PR.
